title: Silver Blaze
description: A mystery involving the disappearance of the racehorse Silver Blaze and the murder of its trainer, Hall Tyson, set in the moors of Dartmoor.
intro_narrative: Sherlock Harris and Dr. Page travel to Dartmoor to investigate the mysterious disappearance of the racehorse Silver Blaze and the murder of its trainer, Hall Tyson. The case involves a web of deceit, hidden motives, and a surprising culprit.

required_evidence: Horse tracks leading to Mapleton stables
required_motive: Hall Tyson's financial troubles due to a secret second life
Attempt to sabotage Silver Blaze for betting gains

phases.name: Arrival in Dartmoor
phases.objective: Investigate the initial crime scene and interview key witnesses.

phases.name: Exploring the Moor
phases.objective: Search the moor for clues and track the movements of Silver Blaze.

phases.name: Uncovering Secrets
phases.objective: Delve into Hall Tyson's hidden life and motives.

phases.name: The Final Revelation
phases.objective: Confront the truth and reveal the culprit at the Wessex Cup.

sherlock_harris.persona: Sharp, analytical, and observant. Speaks in a precise and logical manner, often with a touch of dry humor.
sherlock_harris.abilities: Master of deduction, keen observer of details, and expert in forensic analysis.

conditional_behaviors.reaction: Follows the horse tracks to Mapleton stables, confronting Walken Arnold about Silver Blaze's whereabouts.

dr_page.persona: Curious, methodical, and occasionally skeptical. Acts as the audience surrogate, asking questions to clarify Harris's deductions.
dr_page.abilities: Medical expertise, keen observer, and reliable chronicler of events.

colonel_atkinson.persona: Proud, authoritative, and somewhat dismissive of others' opinions. Deeply concerned about his horse and reputation.

knowledge_about_others.hall_tyson: Trusted trainer with a flawless record until recently.
knowledge_about_others.walken_arnold: Rival trainer with a shady reputation.

colonel_atkinson.secret: Unaware of Tyson's double life and financial troubles.

inspector_miller.persona: Competent but lacks imagination. Follows procedure meticulously and is eager to solve the case.
inspector_miller.abilities: Police procedural expertise, evidence collection, and interrogation skills.

ohara_lautner.persona: Nervous, loyal to Tyson, and eager to prove his innocence. Speaks in a thick Devonshire accent.

knowledge_about_others.portman_blunt: Recognizes him as the stranger who visited the stables.
knowledge_about_others.hall_tyson: Admires him but is unaware of his secrets.

ohara_lautner.secret: Drugged by Tyson to incapacitate him for the night.

jason_lawrence.persona: Observant, talkative, and slightly naive. Provides key details about the night of the crime.

knowledge_about_others.portman_blunt: Saw him the night of the murder and was offered money to deliver a note.
knowledge_about_others.mrs_tyson: Knows she is hiding something about her husband.

jason_lawrence.secret: Saw Portman Blunt but did not report the full details to the police.

walken_arnold.persona: Bullying, cowardly, and sneaky. Quick to anger but easily intimidated when confronted.

knowledge_about_others.hall_tyson: Despised him and saw him as a rival.

walken_arnold.secret: Hid Silver Blaze at Mapleton stables to sabotage the race.

conditional_behaviors.reaction: Admits to hiding Silver Blaze after Harris describes his actions in detail.

portman_blunt.persona: Charming, manipulative, and defensive. Speaks in a polished, educated manner but is quick to anger when accused.

knowledge_about_others.hall_tyson: Saw him as an obstacle to his betting schemes.
knowledge_about_others.ohara_lautner: Attempted to bribe him the night of the murder.

portman_blunt.secret: Involved in betting schemes but innocent of the murder.

mrs_tyson.persona: Haggard, grief-stricken, and defensive. Speaks in a quiet, reserved manner but reveals key details when pressed.

knowledge_about_others.hall_tyson: Knew about his financial troubles but not the extent of his double life.
knowledge_about_others.madame_teller: Unaware of her husband's visits to the milliner.

mrs_tyson.secret: Aware of her husband's financial troubles but not his criminal actions.

madame_teller.persona: Elegant, professional, and discreet. Speaks in a refined manner and is protective of her clients' privacy.

knowledge_about_others.hall_tyson: Recognized him as a customer under the name 'Bell' with an expensive wife.

madame_teller.secret: Knew about Tyson's double life but did not disclose it to authorities.

kings_pyland_stables.description: A small, grey-tiled out-building where Silver Blaze and other horses are trained. The stables are locked at night, and a stable lad sleeps here each night to guard the horses.
kings_pyland_stables.setting: The stables are dimly lit, with the scent of hay and horses filling the air. Stalls line the walls, and a small loft above the harness-room houses the other stable lads.
clues: Horse stall is empty, indicating Silver Blaze's disappearance.
Lautner is found in a stupor, drugged by opium-laced curried mutton.
The stable door was locked from the inside before Lautner left to chase the stranger.

people.name: O'hara Lautner
people.description: A young stable lad with a nervous demeanor. He is currently in a stupor from the drugged mutton.
people.notes: Drugged by Hall Tyson to incapacitate him for the night. Knows about the stranger (Portman Blunt) who visited the stables.

objects.name: Stable Door
objects.description: A sturdy wooden door with a lock. It was locked from the inside before Lautner left to chase the stranger.
objects.notes: Locked state suggests the intruder had a key or was let in by someone familiar.

objects.name: Silver Blaze's Stall
objects.description: An empty stall where Silver Blaze was kept. The straw is disturbed, and there are signs of a struggle.
objects.notes: Silver Blaze's disappearance is the central mystery. The stall shows signs of forced exit.

objects.name: Dish of Curried Mutton
objects.description: A dish of curried mutton left for Lautner. It contains traces of powdered opium.
objects.notes: Key clue indicating Tyson's involvement in drugging Lautner.

objects.name: Water Tap
objects.description: A tap providing water for the stables. Lautner was instructed not to drink anything else.
objects.notes: Explains why no liquid was brought to Lautner, making the drugged mutton more suspicious.

tysons_villa.description: A small, neat villa where Hall Tyson and his wife lived. The villa is located about 200 yards from the stables and is surrounded by a quiet, lonely moor.
tysons_villa.setting: The villa is cozy but sparsely furnished. The atmosphere is tense, with signs of Tyson's recent departure on the night of the murder.
clues: Tyson's overcoat was found flapping from a furze-bush near the moor hollow.
Mrs. Tyson woke to find her husband dressing at 1 AM, claiming anxiety about the horses.
Tyson's ivory-handled knife was found on the dressing table, taken in haste.

people.name: Mrs. Tyson
people.description: A haggard woman with a grief-stricken expression. She is defensive but provides key details about her husband's actions.
people.notes: Unaware of her husband's double life but knows about his financial troubles.

people.name: Jason Lawrence
people.description: A young maid with an observant eye. She is talkative and provides details about the night of the murder.
people.notes: Saw Portman Blunt the night of the murder and was offered money to deliver a note.

objects.name: Dressing Table
objects.description: A small table where Tyson kept personal items. His ivory-handled knife was found here.
objects.notes: The knife's presence suggests Tyson took it in haste, possibly for a delicate operation.

objects.name: Ivory-Handled Knife
objects.description: A delicate, inflexible knife marked Weiss & Co., London. It is stained with blood.
objects.notes: Used for delicate operations, suggesting Tyson's plan to sabotage Silver Blaze.

objects.name: Milliner's Bill
objects.description: A bill for 37 pounds 15 shillings from Madame Teller of Bond Street, addressed to Dunst Bell.
objects.notes: Indicates Tyson's double life and financial troubles.

objects.name: Hall Tyson's Overcoat
objects.description: A large mackintosh found flapping from a furze-bush near the moor hollow.
objects.notes: Suggests Tyson was in the hollow and removed his coat for a delicate task.

moor_hollow.description: A bowl-shaped depression in the moor where Hall Tyson's body was found. The ground is trampled, and Tyson's overcoat was found flapping from a nearby furze-bush.
moor_hollow.setting: The hollow is surrounded by faded ferns and brambles, with a somber atmosphere. The ground is muddy, preserving tracks and clues.
clues: Tyson's body was found here with a shattered skull and a knife wound on the thigh.
A red and black silk cravat, identified as Portman Blunt's, was clutched in Tyson's hand.
Horse tracks lead away from the hollow toward Mapleton stables.

objects.name: Furze-Bush
objects.description: A bush where Tyson's overcoat was found flapping. The coat was placed here deliberately.
objects.notes: Suggests Tyson removed his coat for a task and placed it here to keep it dry.

objects.name: Hall Tyson's Body
objects.description: The body of Hall Tyson, with a shattered skull and a knife wound on the thigh. A cravat is clutched in his hand.
objects.notes: The wounds suggest a struggle, and the cravat links Portman Blunt to the scene.

objects.name: Muddy Ground
objects.description: The ground is trampled and muddy, preserving tracks of horses and people.
objects.notes: Key evidence includes horse tracks leading to Mapleton and boot prints matching Walken Arnold.

objects.name: Half-Burned Wax Vesta
objects.description: A half-burned wax vesta found buried in the mud, indicating someone struck a match here.
objects.notes: Suggests Tyson struck a match to perform a delicate operation on Silver Blaze.

mapleton_stables.description: A larger training establishment owned by Lord Hart and managed by Walken Arnold. The stables are located about two miles from King's Pyland.
mapleton_stables.setting: The stables are well-maintained, with a professional atmosphere. The horses are kept in pristine condition, and the staff is disciplined.
clues: Horse tracks lead here from the moor hollow, suggesting Silver Blaze was hidden here.
Walken Arnold's boots match the square-toed prints found near the hollow.
Silver Blaze was found here, disguised with dye to hide its identity.

people.name: Walken Arnold
people.description: A fierce-looking elderly man with a bullying demeanor. He is the trainer at Mapleton stables.
people.notes: Hid Silver Blaze to sabotage the race but was forced to confess when confronted by Harris.

objects.name: Stable Door
objects.description: A sturdy door leading to the stables. It is kept locked at night.
objects.notes: Arnold likely used a key to hide Silver Blaze inside.

objects.name: Disguised Silver Blaze
objects.description: Silver Blaze, disguised with dye to hide its white forehead and mottled leg.
objects.notes: Arnold hid the horse to prevent it from winning the Wessex Cup.

objects.name: Walken Arnold's Boots
objects.description: A pair of boots with square toes, matching the prints found near the moor hollow.
objects.notes: Links Arnold to the scene of the crime and the hiding of Silver Blaze.

tavistock_inn.description: A quaint inn in the town of Tavistock, where visitors and locals gather. It is a hub of gossip and information.
tavistock_inn.setting: The inn is cozy and bustling, with a warm atmosphere. Patrons discuss the latest news, including the Silver Blaze case.
clues: Portman Blunt is staying here, providing an alibi and background for his actions.
Gossip about the case and the involvement of gypsies and rival stables.
Information about the betting odds for the Wessex Cup.

people.name: Portman Blunt
people.description: A man of gentlemanly bearing with a charming but defensive demeanor. He is a bookmaker with a shady reputation.
people.notes: Innocent of the murder but involved in betting schemes. Dropped his cravat at the scene.

objects.name: Portman Blunt's Betting Book
objects.description: A book showing bets placed against Silver Blaze, totaling five thousand pounds.
objects.notes: Provides motive for Blunt's interest in the horse's disappearance.

objects.name: Red and Black Silk Cravat
objects.description: A cravat identified as Portman Blunt's, found clutched in Tyson's hand.
objects.notes: Links Blunt to the crime scene, though he claims it was stolen.

objects.name: Inn Register
objects.description: A register showing Portman Blunt's stay at the inn, including dates and room number.
objects.notes: Provides Blunt's alibi and timeline for the night of the murder.

tavistock_police_station.description: A small police station in Tavistock where Inspector Miller is investigating the case. It is a hub for evidence and interrogations.
tavistock_police_station.setting: The station is functional and orderly, with a desk for the inspector and a holding cell for suspects.
clues: Evidence collected from the crime scene, including Tyson's belongings and the cravat.
Records of Portman Blunt's arrest and interrogation.

people.notes: Leading the investigation and focused on Portman Blunt as the prime suspect.

gypsy_encampment.description: A temporary encampment of gypsies on the moor, suspected of involvement in Silver Blaze's disappearance.
gypsy_encampment.setting: The encampment is rustic and nomadic, with tents and campfires. The atmosphere is mysterious and secretive.
clues: Gypsies were encamped near the crime scene on the night of the murder but left the next day.
No direct evidence links them to Silver Blaze's disappearance.
Gossip suggests they may have been involved in hiding the horse.

objects.name: Campfire

objects.notes: No evidence of Silver Blaze or involvement in the crime.

winchester_racecourse.setting: The racecourse is bustling with activity, with spectators, bookmakers, and horses preparing for the race. The atmosphere is electric.
